claim: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark Observation Deck 2026 pricing: non-peak adult S$35 / concession S$31; peak adult S$39 / concession S$35; family of four S$110 non-peak.
quote: Non-peak: Adult S$35, Concession S$31, Family package (2 adults & 2 children) S$110. Peak: Adult S$39, Concession S$35, Family package S$126.

claim: Gardens by the Bay Flower Dome + Cloud Forest combo (with Jurassic World: The Experience) is S$46 adult non-resident, S$34 resident; open 9am–9pm with last admission 8:30pm.
quote: Daily: 9.00am – 9.00pm (Last admission at 8.30pm). Non-Resident Adult: $46, Child $32. Singapore Resident Adult: $34, Senior $29, Child $26.

claim: Garden Rhapsody at Supertree Grove runs free daily at 7:45pm and 8:45pm with a rotating monthly theme.
quote: Daily, 7.45pm & 8.45pm. Free admission. Supertree Grove. Garden Rhapsody adopts a different theme every month.

claim: Spectra at Marina Bay Sands Event Plaza is a free 15-minute show running 8pm and 9pm Sun–Thu, plus a 10pm show on Fri/Sat.
quote: Spectra runs daily with shows at 8pm & 9pm Sunday–Thursday, and 8pm, 9pm & 10pm on Friday & Saturday. The nightly show is free and open to all.

claim: Singapore Flyer is widely tagged a tourist trap: shorter than MBS, ~10 minutes at the highest point, and roughly S$40 per person; SkyPark and the Flyer are both flagged as overpriced view-only experiences with cheaper alternatives like CÉ LA VI, LAVO, Supertree Observatory (S$14) and Pinnacle@Duxton (S$6).
quote: Singapore Flyer ... is SHORTER than Marina Bay Sands ... you only get to enjoy the highest point for about 10 minutes ... SkyPark can feel overpriced when all you get to do is see the view.

claim: Singapore Flyer operates 10am–10pm; the Time Capsule pre-boarding gallery closed for upgrades in April 2025 with relocated entry, reopening August 2025.
quote: Singapore Flyer is open from 10:00-22:00 ... The Time Capsule was closed for upgrading works starting April 28, 2025 ... set to reopen in August 2025.

claim: Merlion Park is free, open 24/7, and the 8.6m / 70-tonne statue offers iconic skyline photos of Marina Bay Sands and the Flyer; visitors typically spend 15–30 minutes.
quote: Merlion Park is 100% free, 24 hours, with no tickets or gates ... The Merlion statue stands at 8.6 metres high and weighs 70 tonnes ... Many visitors suggest spending 15 to 30 minutes for photo opportunities.

claim: ArtScience Museum charges roughly S$28–S$56 depending on exhibitions and resident status, with 21 galleries and signature shows like teamLab's Future World plus 2026 specials (Mirror Mirror, NOX, Into the Ocean).
quote: Tourist tickets are priced at S$56, while Singapore residents enjoy a discounted rate of S$27 ... Ticket prices start from S$28.00 ... 21 gallery spaces ... Future World ... curated by teamLab.

claim: Consensus pick: Cloud Forest's 35m indoor waterfall and misting walkways deliver the bigger 'wow' for time-pressed visitors, while Flower Dome rewards slower botanical browsing; both side-by-side take ~2 hours.
quote: Cloud Forest's 35-m waterfall, misting shows, and elevated walks deliver instant wow with a compact route ... Flower Dome is gentler and spacious ... do both—they sit side by side and take ~2 hours combined.

claim: To avoid crowds at the conservatories, visit early in the morning right at the 9am opening; weekends and holidays produce heavy queues, especially around Garden Rhapsody showtimes.
quote: Morning hours because it's not as crowded and you can see the blooms in natural light ... going early in the morning is recommended so you can explore the massive place without feeling rushed and beat the tourist crowds.

claim: The MICHELIN Bib Gourmand Singapore 2025 selection honors 89 eateries with 11 new entries, over 70% of which are street food stalls.
quote: This year's Bib Gourmand selection honors 89 eateries — from iconic hawker stalls to neighborhood treasures — that serve up delicious meals without the hefty price tag.

claim: New 2025 Bib Gourmand hawker stalls include Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow, Nam Sing Hokkien Fried Mee and To-Ricos Kway Chap at Old Airport Road, Song Kee Teochew Fish Porridge at Newton, and Ji Ji Noodle House at Hong Lim.
quote: Among the nine additions this year are Kitchenman Nasi Lemak, Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow, Nam Sing Hokkien Fried Mee, Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh, Song Kee Teochew Fish Porridge, Wok Hei Hor Fun and To-Ricos Kway Chap.

claim: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice at Maxwell Food Centre (#01-10/11) opens daily 10am to 7:30pm with chicken rice priced from S$5 small to S$8.80 large.
quote: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice... 1 Kadayanallur St, #01-10/11 Maxwell Food Centre

claim: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice holds Bib Gourmand recognition in the 2025 Michelin Guide Singapore.
quote: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice... Bib Gourmand: good quality, good value cooking

claim: Lau Pa Sat operates 24 hours and its open-air Satay Street section runs from 7pm on weekdays and 3pm on weekends until roughly 3am.
quote: Satay Street operates weekdays from 7 PM and weekends and public holidays from 3 PM... Satay stalls are open late (until 1 or 3 AM)

claim: Lau Pa Sat satay sticks cost roughly S$0.70–1.00 for chicken or beef and S$1.50–2.00 for prawns, with stalls 7 and 8 the most famous.
quote: Expect to pay around SGD 0.70–1.00 per stick for chicken or beef, and SGD 1.50–2.00 for prawns... Stalls 7 & 8 are the most famous

claim: Chef Chan Hon Meng's Liao Fan Hong Kong Soya Sauce Chicken Rice & Noodle in Chinatown Complex was the first hawker stall awarded a Michelin star (2016) and lost it in the 2021 guide.
quote: Hawker Chan – previously known as Liao Fan Hong Kong Soya Sauce Chicken Rice & Noodles – was no longer listed... the first Singapore hawker to be awarded a Michelin star in 2016, lost it after five years in 2021.

claim: Singapore's hawker culture was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity on 16 December 2020, the city-state's first such listing.
quote: The IGC announced the successful inscription of Hawker Culture in Singapore on the Representative List on 16 December 2020 at approximately 10.09pm (UTC +08:00).

claim: Old Airport Road Food Centre highlights include Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow (Bib Gourmand) for wok-hei char kway teow, Wang Wang Crispy Curry Puff, Roast Paradise KL-style char siew (S$4.50/$5.50), and Hokkien Mee.
quote: Lao Fu Zi is known for its char kway teow with strong wok hei (breath of wok) and is listed on the Michelin Bib gourmand.

claim: Newton Food Centre's Alliance Seafood is a Michelin Bib Gourmand stall famed for chilli crab (seasonal pricing); the centre is best visited 6–7pm or after 9:30pm to dodge queues.
quote: Alliance Seafood has been serving up seafood delights for over three decades, and consistently earns the prestigious Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition year after year.

claim: Tiong Bahru Market reopened in July 2025 after a three-month renovation; standout stalls include Bib Gourmand Jian Bo Shui Kueh (founded 1958, S$3.50 for five pieces of chwee kueh), Hui Ji Fishball Noodles and Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice.
quote: Tiong Bahru Food Centre reopened its doors in July 2025 after a three-month renovation.

claim: Amoy Street Food Centre concentrates the most Michelin-listed stalls of any Singapore hawker centre, including A Noodle Story (Singapore-style ramen S$10.80), Han Kee Fish Soup, Hong Kee Beef Noodles and J2 Famous Crispy Curry Puff.
quote: A Noodle Story... With 7 consecutive Michelin Bib Gourmand awards under its belt, this coveted stall commands a queue as soon as it opens shop.

claim: Chinatown Complex Food Centre is Singapore's largest hawker centre with about 195–260 operating stalls; Bib Gourmand picks include Lian He Ben Ji Claypot Rice (#02-198/199) and Xiu Ji Ikan Bilis Yong Tau Foo.
quote: Chinatown Complex Food Centre, found in the heart of Smith Street, is Singapore's largest hawker centre.

claim: Visit Singapore publishes a self-guided Chinatown walking route covering Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Sri Mariamman Temple and Pagoda Street with map and MRT info.
quote: A self-guided Chinatown Singapore walking tour map features main attractions including temples, Pagoda Street, hawker centres, museums, and nearby MRT stations.

claim: The Buddha Tooth Relic Temple is a five-storey Tang-dynasty-style complex built in 2007, open daily 9am-6pm with free admission.
quote: The Buddha Tooth Relic Temple is a five-storey Tang-dynasty-style complex housing what is believed to be a sacred tooth relic of the Gautama Buddha, built in 2007 and funded by donations from the Singapore Buddhist community.

claim: Thian Hock Keng on Telok Ayer Street is Singapore's oldest Chinese temple, built 1839-42 without nails and dedicated to sea-goddess Mazu.
quote: Thian Hock Keng is Singapore's oldest Chinese temple, located in the heart of Chinatown with rich history and cultural significance. The temple, which means 'Temple of Heavenly Happiness,' dates back to the 1800s and is dedicated to Mazu, a Chinese sea goddess.

claim: The former House of Tan Teng Niah (1900) is the last surviving Chinese villa in Little India, now a brightly-painted heritage photo stop on Kerbau Road.
quote: Built in 1900, the former house of Tan Teng Niah is the last surviving Chinese villa in Little India. Tan Teng Niah was a towkay (Chinese businessman of good standing) who owned several sweet-making factories along Serangoon Road that used sugarcane to produce sweets.

claim: The Indian Heritage Centre on Campbell Lane is open Tue-Sun 10am-6pm with last admission 5:30pm, closed Mondays including public holidays.
quote: Tuesday – Sunday, 10am to 6pm (Last admission at 5:30pm). The centre is closed every Monday, including public holidays which fall on Monday unless otherwise stated.

claim: Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple, established 1855, opens daily 5.30am-noon and 4-9pm with a midday closure 12:15-4pm; shoes must be removed.
quote: The opening hours are Mon–Sun 5.30am–noon, 4–9pm. The temple is closed between 12:15 and 4 pm... established in 1855, making it one of Singapore's oldest houses of worship.

claim: The Malay Heritage Centre at Istana Kampong Glam has reopened after its extensive revamp; permanent galleries run Tue-Sun 10am-6pm and the compound 8am-9pm.
quote: After an extensive revamp and restoration, we are so glad to finally have our doors open again. Permanent Galleries: Tuesday–Sunday, 10am–6pm (closed Mondays); Compound: Tuesday–Sunday, 8am–9pm.

claim: Haji Lane is a 250m strip of shophouses packed with indie boutiques, cafes, murals and bars; named indie stores include RE.DRMG, VINTAGEWKND, PLOP APPARELS, Wicked Laundry and Matter Prints.
quote: Haji Lane is a 250-metre strip of shophouses in Kampong Glam — indie boutiques, specialty cafes, street murals, and bars all packed into one narrow alley... indie boutiques like RE.DRMG, VINTAGEWKND, and PLOP APPARELS.

claim: Sultan Mosque sits at 3 Muscat Street; the original 1824 building was demolished and the current dome-and-minaret structure was completed in 1932.
quote: The Sultan Mosque is located at 3 Muscat Street and is the focal point of the historic Kampong Glam area. The original structure was demolished about a century after the mosque was first built in 1824 to make way for the current building, which was completed in 1932.

claim: Tiong Bahru's Streamline Moderne walk-up flats (Singapore's first public housing, 1930s) cluster around Seng Poh Road, Yong Siak Street, Moh Guan Terrace and Tiong Poh Road with curved corners and horizontal lines suited to the tropics.
quote: The core of the estate — concentrated around Seng Poh Road, Yong Siak Street, Moh Guan Terrace, and Tiong Poh Road — is a remarkably intact collection of Streamline Moderne residential blocks from the 1930s... favouring horizontal lines, curved corners, and aerodynamic forms designed for tropical ventilation.

claim: Tiong Bahru Bakery on Eng Hoon Street is famed for its kouign-amann and croissants; nearby Cat Socrates at 78 Yong Siak Street stocks local books, Peranakan tiles and indie crafts after BooksActually moved online in 2022.
quote: Tiong Bahru Bakery on Eng Hoon Street — serving croissants that people consistently describe as the best in Singapore... Cat Socrates at 78 Yong Siak Street is one of the most beloved independent shops in Singapore — a browsing paradise of local books, Singaporean design pieces, Peranakan tiles, quirky homewares, and indie crafts.

claim: Koon Seng Road's pastel Peranakan shophouses are a roughly 50m stretch and Katong/Joo Chiat was Singapore's first Heritage Town (2011), with facades legally protected from alteration.
quote: At the intersection with Koon Seng Road, you'll step into one of Singapore's most iconic streets, lined with Peranakan shophouses. Though it's only around 50 metres long... The area was designated a national heritage conservation area in 1993 and named Singapore's first Heritage Town in 2011.

claim: The Katong Antique House is a private Peranakan museum-shophouse founded by the late Peter Wee, a 4th-generation Peranakan, and now run by Angeline Kong and Eric Ang.
quote: The Katong Antique House was owned by the late Peter Wee, a 4th generation Peranakan and former president of The Peranakan Association Singapore... The museum is currently led by Angeline Kong and Eric Ang.

claim: The Katong laksa rivalry pits 328 Katong Laksa (creamy, seafood-heavy, founded 1998 after taking over Marine Parade Laksa's premises) against Janggut/Marine Parade Laksa (lighter broth, more laksa-leaf), tracing back to a 1998 rent dispute.
quote: Mrs Teo, the landlady of 49 East Coast Road, decided to cash in on the success of Marine Parade Laksa and put her rental prices up in 1998, forcing the Ng brothers to move out. The premises were taken over by Nancy Lim (now Nancy Koh), who re-named the coffee shop 328 Laksa.

claim: Free walking tours in Singapore are either tip-based group walks (SGD 15-30 tip suggested) or genuinely free National Heritage Board self-guided trails, covering Chinatown, Little India, Kampong Glam, Tiong Bahru and the Civic District.
quote: Tip-based free tours are led by local guides who walk you through a neighbourhood for no upfront fee, with visitors typically tipping SGD $15–$30 per person. Additionally, self-guided free tours are genuinely zero-cost, where you follow a heritage trail map provided by the Singapore Tourism Board.

claim: Chinatown free walking tours typically start at Telok Ayer MRT and include Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Sri Mariamman Temple (Singapore's oldest Hindu shrine, 1827) and Fuk Tak Chi Museum.
quote: Tours starting at Telok Ayer MRT unpack the history of Chinese immigrants, with stops including Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Sri Mariamman Temple (Singapore's oldest Hindu shrine, built in 1827), and the Fuk Tak Chi Museum.

claim: Singapore Botanic Gardens is free to enter; only the National Orchid Garden is ticketed, open daily 08:30–19:00 with last entry 18:00.
quote: The National Orchid Garden opening hours are daily from 8:30 AM to 7 PM. The last entry to the National Orchid Garden and its attractions is at 6 PM, daily.

claim: National Orchid Garden 2026 admission is SGD 15 for foreign adults, SGD 5 for local adults, SGD 1 for local students/seniors, and free for children under 12.
quote: Adults: SGD 5.00; Students: SGD 1.00; Senior citizens (60 years and above): SGD 1.00; Children below 12 years: FREE ... Foreign adults: S$15

claim: Rainforest Wild Asia is Mandai's newest adventure-based wildlife park with limited daily capacity; pre-booking is strongly recommended as same-day tickets can sell out by mid-morning on weekends and holidays.
quote: Rainforest Wild Asia is one of Mandai's newest and most in-demand attractions with limited daily capacity, and pre-booking online is highly recommended, especially on weekends, holidays, and school breaks, as same-day tickets may sell out by mid-morning.

claim: A Mandai multi-attraction bundle is SGD 128 for adults (usual price SGD 246), covering Night Safari plus one choice of Singapore Zoo, River Wonders, Bird Paradise or Rainforest Wild Adventure.
quote: a multi-attraction bundle is available at S$128 for adults (U.P. S$246), which includes Night Safari and a choice of Singapore Zoo, River Wonders, Bird Paradise OR Rainforest Wild Adventure

claim: Singapore Zoo single-park adult admission is SGD 48 and Night Safari from SGD 53 in 2026.
quote: Night Safari: Adult tickets start at SGD 53 ... Singapore Zoo: SGD 48 for adults

claim: The MacRitchie TreeTop Walk is open Tuesday–Friday 09:00–17:00 and from 08:30 on weekends (closed Mondays), with last entry at 16:45.
quote: The TreeTop Walk is open from 9am to 5pm on Tuesdays to Fridays and from 8.30am on weekends (closed on Mondays); the last entry is at 4.45pm.

claim: The MacRitchie TreeTop suspension bridge spans 250m connecting Bukit Peirce and Bukit Kalang, reached via a 4.5km walk from the Lornie Road entrance (1–2 hours one way) on the broader 11km nature trail.
quote: The TreeTop Walk spans approximately 250 meters, connecting the two highest points in MacRitchie — Bukit Peirce and Bukit Kalang ... about a 4.5km walk from the main MacRitchie Reservoir Park entrance at Lornie Road (about 1-2 hours depending on how fast you walk). It's part of the 11-kilometer MacRitchie Nature Trail.

claim: Long-tailed macaques along the MacRitchie trail are fearless; visitors should not feed them, scream, or use flash photography.
quote: MacRitchie Reservoir's macaques are quite fearless, so it's important to use common sense and follow park regulations to not antagonise them (don't feed them, don't scream at them, don't use flash photography).

claim: Henderson Waves is Singapore's tallest pedestrian bridge, a 274m undulating span with seven curved 'ribs' that double as shelters and alcoves.
quote: The iconic Henderson Waves is a distinct 274m-long pedestrian bridge with a unique wave-like structure, and is the tallest pedestrian bridge in Singapore. A series of seven undulating "ribs" double up as alcoves and provide shelter to park users looking for rest.

claim: The Southern Ridges is a 10km trail linking four parks; both routes start at HarbourFront MRT Exit D and take 3–5 hours; Henderson Waves is LED-lit nightly 19:00–02:00.
quote: Both route A and B start at Harbourfront MRT station Exit D ... Both routes take an estimated 3-5 hours to complete ... admire how attractive it looks when lit up with LED lights from 7pm to 2am daily.

claim: The Pulau Ubin bumboat from Changi Point costs SGD 4 per person (cash, plus SGD 4 surcharge for a bicycle), runs 06:00–19:00 daily, departs when 9–12 passengers board, and crosses in about 15 minutes.
quote: The Pulau Ubin ferry costs S$4 per person per trip, and you pay the boat operator directly in cash ... The bumboats run from 6am to 7pm daily, and they don't have a fixed schedule. They leave whenever there are 9 to 12 passengers on board ... The boat ride takes about 15 minutes

claim: Pulau Ubin's standout sights include Chek Jawa Wetlands boardwalks, Puaka Hill summit, Butterfly Hill, Ketam Mountain Bike Park, and cycle rentals around SGD 15–25 per day.
quote: At the top of the list of must-see attractions on Pulau Ubin are the Chek Jawa Wetlands ... hiking to the summit of Puaka Hill ... Ketam Mountain Bike Park ... The rental fee varies but a typical cost is around S$15-25 for a full day

claim: Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve hosts migratory shorebirds from August to April, including Whimbrels, Common Greenshanks, Pacific Golden Plovers and Lesser Sand Plovers; over 200 bird species have been recorded.
quote: During migratory season from August to April, catch sight of flocks of Whimbrels, Common Greenshanks, Common Redshanks, Pacific Golden Plovers ... Over 200 species of birds have been spotted at the Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve

claim: Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve is free to enter, open daily 07:00–19:00 with last entry 18:00, and covers more than 200 hectares of mangrove habitat along the East Asian–Australasian Flyway.
quote: The reserve operates daily from 7 AM to 7 PM, with last entry at 6 PM ... spanning over 200 hectares of mangrove habitat and serving as a vital stopover for migratory birds along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway.

claim: Bukit Timah Nature Reserve is open daily 07:00–19:00 and offers multiple trails up Singapore's 163m natural summit; the main red trail to the top takes 30–45 minutes.
quote: The hike to the summit takes 30 to 45 minutes via the red trail at a regular walking pace, with the descent taking 20 to 30 minutes ... The reserve is open from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM daily.

claim: Coney Island Park is open 07:00–19:00 (gates close at 19:00), has West and East entrances, no on-island carparks, and a 2.5km park connector ideal for cycling; visitors should avoid feeding monkeys.
quote: The park operates from 7am to 7pm (gates will be closed at 7pm). You can enter the park via 2 entrances: the West entrance (near Punggol Point Walk and Punggol Promenade) or the East entrance (near Lorong Halus Wetland) ... Cycle along the 2.5km Coney Island Park Connector

claim: Coney Island has recorded more than 80 species of resident and migratory birds and features the Casuarina Exploration playground; visitors are warned about sandflies and should bring water as there are no food facilities on-island.
quote: More than 80 species of resident and migratory birds have been spotted at this park ... Wear long pants and covered shoes for protection from insects such as sandflies. Once you get on to Coney Island itself, there aren't any facilities for food

claim: Universal Studios Singapore adult tickets start from S$83 (off-peak) and S$86 (peak) with child tickets from S$62, and Minion Land is one of the headline zones.
quote: Universal Studios Singapore Tickets | From S$83 | Minion Land & More

claim: Illumination's Minion Land officially opened at Universal Studios Singapore on February 14, 2025.
quote: Illumination's Minion Land to Officially Open at Universal Studios Singapore on February 14, 2025

claim: Minion Land features the exclusive Buggie Boogie dance-party carousel plus Super Hungry Food Stand, Despicable Me Minion Mayhem and live street shows.
quote: Exclusive to Universal Studios Singapore is Buggie Boogie – the first-ever Minion dance party-themed carousel – and Super Hungry Food Stand

claim: S.E.A. Aquarium closed 30 April 2025 and reopened on 24 July 2025 as the Singapore Oceanarium, roughly three times larger with 22 themed zones.
quote: S.E.A. Aquarium ceased operations on 30 April 2025 for rebranding and expansion works, and reopened as Singapore Oceanarium on 24 July 2025.

claim: The new Oceanarium showcases over 40,000 marine animals across 22 zones including Ocean Wonders, Ancient Waters with life-sized animatronics, and Singapore's Coast mangrove recreation.
quote: the refreshed attraction is three times larger than before, with 22 themed zones spotlighting different aspects of marine life

claim: Singapore Cable Car runs 8.45am–10pm daily with adult fare S$29 / child S$18, and ticket holders can upgrade one leg to a SkyOrb chrome-finished spherical cabin with glass floor for S$15.
quote: Admission: S$29/Adult; S$18/Child ... upgrade one-way of their round trip to a SkyOrb Cabin for $15

claim: Sentosa Express monorail entry to the island costs S$4 and includes unlimited rides within Sentosa; walking via the Sentosa Boardwalk and Gateway is free.
quote: Pay S$4 island admission (includes unlimited rides within Sentosa) when using the Sentosa Express monorail

claim: Skyline Luge offers Night Luge sessions exclusively on Fridays and Saturdays from 7pm to 9pm, with a Night Luge Duo Bundle giving S$16 off and a free digital photo.
quote: Night Luge is available exclusively on Fridays & Saturdays

claim: Standard daytime Skyline Luge tickets start from S$31.50 per person.
quote: Tickets & Packages | Skyline Luge Singapore Pricing

claim: Mega Adventure's MegaZip zipline standard price is around S$66 with an Early Bird Special at S$59 available from 11am to 2pm daily.
quote: Grab your MegaZip tickets for just $59 (U.P. $66)

claim: Pulau Palawan, linked to Palawan Beach by a suspension bridge, has a Sentosa-erected sign declaring it the 'southernmost point of Continental Asia' and features two lookout towers.
quote: There is a sign on the islet erected by the Sentosa Development Corporation declaring that it is the "southernmost point of Continental Asia"

claim: Adventure Cove Waterpark tickets start from S$35 via the official RWS site.
quote: Book Adventure Cove Waterpark Tickets - Starts from SGD 35

claim: Wild Wild Wet at Pasir Ris is Singapore's largest mainland waterpark with 15 attractions including Kraken Racers, Free Fall and a KidZ Zone; tickets start from about S$26.
quote: Singapore's Premier Water Theme Park and Aqua Park

claim: SuperPark Singapore at Suntec City reopened 25 May 2025 with 34 activities across 25,000 sq ft over two levels, including 13 new installations like Twin Slide Tower and Airbag Donut Slide.
quote: SuperPark Singapore is located on the first floor of Suntec City Mall and reopened on 25 May 2025

claim: MINT Museum of Toys on Seah Street is the largest vintage toy museum in Asia with around 8,500 toys on display spanning the late 19th century to modern pop culture, and offers AR experiences for kids aged 4–12.
quote: Children's Museum Singapore - Kid's Friendly Museum Exhibition

claim: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025 placed five Singapore bars in the top 50: Jigger & Pony (No.3), Offtrack (No.23), Nutmeg & Clove (No.24), Cat Bite Club (No.44) and Native (No.45).
quote: Jigger & Pony is crowned The Best Bar in Singapore and third in Asia – that's seven years straight of appearing in Asia's 50 Best Bars' top 10 ranking.

claim: Singapore's extended 51-100 representatives include Side Door (53), Sago House (56), Origin Bar (60), Night Hawk (77), Employees Only (89) and Fura (95).
quote: Singapore claims six places on the 51-100 list, with Side Door, a new entrant, leading the pack at No.53... Sago House at No.56, followed by Origin Bar (No.60), Night Hawk (No.77), and Employees Only (No.89), culminating with Fura at No.95.

claim: Singapore's World's 50 Best Bars 2025 entries are Jigger & Pony at No.9 and Nutmeg & Clove at No.50, with Native at No.84 on the extended list.
quote: Jigger & Pony is the best bar in Singapore, securing its spot within the top 10 at No. 9... Nutmeg & Clove also lands itself a spot on the World's 50 Best Bars 2025 list at No. 50.

claim: The Long Bar at Raffles Singapore is the birthplace of the Singapore Sling, created around 1915 by Hainanese bartender Ngiam Tong Boon.
quote: The Singapore Sling is a gin-based cocktail that was created around 1915 by a Hainanese bartender named Ngiam Tong Boon, right here at the Raffles Hotel's Long Bar.

claim: A Singapore Sling at the Long Bar costs S$39 before service charge and tax, roughly S$47 all-in.
quote: the price for a Singapore Sling at the Long Bar is S$39, before service charge and taxes. With the service charge and taxes included, this comes to approximately S$47

claim: Atlas occupies the Art Deco lobby of Parkview Square in Bugis and houses a soaring eight-metre gin tower stocked with over 1,300 labels.
quote: Atlas is located in the lobby of Parkview Square in Bugis, also known as Singapore's 'Gotham Building,' and features soaring ceilings, gleaming gold, and an iconic eight-metre gin tower

claim: Manhattan at Conrad Singapore Orchard launched its 2025 'Seasons of Manhattan' menu of 31 cocktails inspired by New York's four seasons, and houses the world's first in-hotel rickhouse.
quote: Seasons of Manhattan... presents 31 cocktails capturing the essence of Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter in New York City.

claim: Native on Amoy Street is a three-storey shophouse with a ground-floor restaurant, second-floor cocktail bar and third-floor fermentation lab, focused on regional Southeast Asian spirits and ingredients.
quote: The establishment comprises a restaurant on the first floor, a cocktail bar on the second and a fermentation lab on the third

claim: CÉ LA VI sits on the 57th floor atop Marina Bay Sands with modern Asian flavours and a SkyBar.
quote: Perched on the 57th floor of Marina Bay Sands, CÉ LA VI takes modern Asian flavours and electrifying entertainment to the highest level.

claim: LeVeL33 at Marina Bay Financial Centre is billed as the world's highest urban craft microbrewery, brewing lagers, ales, stouts and wheat beers on-site.
quote: LeVeL33 holds the title of the world's highest urban microbrewery, brewing its own lagers, ales, stouts, and wheat beers on-site at Marina Bay Financial Centre.

claim: 1-Altitude on the 63rd floor of One Raffles Place is listed as closed as of the rooftop guide's October 2025 update; 1-Group has shifted its rooftop play to 1-Altitude Coast on Sentosa.
quote: 1-Altitude Closed

claim: Haw Par Villa offers free outdoor park entry (9am–8pm), but the outdoor park is closed from 8 December 2025 until further notice; only the ticketed Hell's Museum (from S$20) remains open.
quote: The park will be closed from 8 December 2025 until further notice. Not to worry, Hell's Museum is still open. Tickets to visit Hell's Museum costs from $20

claim: Sembawang Hot Spring Park is Singapore's only natural mainland hot spring, open free daily 7am–7pm with a cascading foot bath and an egg-cooking station at 70°C.
quote: Sembawang Hot Spring Park is Singapore's only hot spring park, set in a rustic, kampung-like setting.

claim: Three-hour kelong boat tours from the northeast coast visit Smith Marine, the country's first floating seafood kelong restaurant, and pass some of Singapore's last remaining stilted fish farms off Pulau Ubin.
quote: an actual visit to Smith Marine Kelong, the first Floating Seafood Restaurant in Singapore located just off the coastal waters of Pulau Ubin

claim: Singapore's 24-hour supper scene anchors on Geylang, where Yong He Eating House (458 Geylang Rd Lor 24A) is famous for mala bak kut teh, alongside 24/7 spots like 89.7 Supper Club and Kazutake Ramen.
quote: 89.7 Supper Club is open 24/7 and offers a wide variety of cuisines... Yong He Eating House at 458 Geylang Road Lor 24A, open 24/7, famous for mala bak kut teh

claim: Sentosa's three southern beaches — Siloso, Palawan and Tanjong — are artificial, reclaimed using sand bought from Indonesia and Malaysia.
quote: These beaches are artificial, reclaimed using sand bought from Indonesia and Malaysia.

claim: Palawan Beach is linked by a wooden suspension bridge to a small islet billed as the Southernmost Point of Continental Asia, with twin viewing towers.
quote: Southernmost Point of Continental Asia

claim: Wave House Sentosa, the FlowRider/FlowBarrel surf venue on Siloso Beach, is listed as CLOSED on Time Out's Singapore directory.
quote: Wave House Sentosa (CLOSED)

claim: Tanjong Beach Club reopened after a four-month facelift with a new wood-fired menu and warmer palette, replacing its earlier pristine-white look after 15 years.
quote: Once known for its pristine white look, Tanjong Beach Club has since swapped that up for warmer, more vibrant shades that instantly modernises the 15-year-old space.

claim: Tanjong Beach Club programmes the chill/luxe end of Sentosa: wood-fired grill, daybeds, sunset cocktails plus Tanjong Rose Club brunch and GAIAVIP house/techno DJ series.
quote: where beach culture, community and soulful experiences collide

claim: Smoke & Mirrors, the rooftop cocktail bar atop National Gallery Singapore, served its last night on 15 March 2025 after nine years when its lease ended.
quote: National Gallery S'pore bar Smoke & Mirrors closing down on Mar. 15 after 9 years

claim: Smoke & Mirrors' programme paired a Padang skyline view with art-driven cocktails — its 'Real Art of Drinking' menus mimicked gallery artworks, the latest being 12 drinks built around a painter's-palette colour wheel.
quote: The current menu showcases 12 cocktails inspired by painter's palette colours

claim: Time Out ranked Smoke & Mirrors the world's #2 rooftop bar in 2024, its highest international accolade before the closure.
quote: Smoke & Mirrors comes in second among the best rooftop bars in the world
